spec_family.name: Interior Drywall Ceiling Repaint
spec_family.description: Combined prime + finish repaint spec for previously painted interior drywall ceiling surfaces in occupied residential homes. Covers condition assessment (visual scan, adhesion test, moisture meter, coating ID), prep remediation (scrape, feather, degloss, spackle, contamination treatment), state-driven primer selection (adhesion, stain-block, mildew-resistant), finish coat application (roll, spray_backroll, spray), interstage inspection/repair, furniture drip protection (in-place), and full-room floor protection. Second interior RP spec (after SF_DRYWALL_WALL_INT_RP). All rates include 15-20% overhead penalty vs wall equivalents.

includes: Condition assessment (visual scan with raking work light, ASTM D3359 adhesion test, moisture meter, coating ID)
EPA Lead-Safe RRP evaluation and containment for pre-1978 homes
Surface contamination treatment (TSP wash for mildew, smoke, water stain, grease)
Mildew/biocide treatment for SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE
Scraping loose and failing ceiling paint (condition-driven intensity)
Feather-sanding all scraped edges (mandatory at all QT)
Deglossing existing ceiling paint surface (chemical preferred overhead — less dust)
Spackle ceiling defects and sand repairs (QT3+)
Caulk assessment and replacement at ceiling-to-wall perimeter joint (QT3+)
State-driven primer selection and application (adhesion, stain-block, mildew-resistant)
Spot priming all spackled/scraped areas
Finish coat application — 1 coat QT2, 2 coats QT3-QT5 (roll, spray_backroll, spray)
Interstage inspection, light sanding (QT4/QT5), and defect repair
Final inspection and touch-up
Full-room floor protection (always — overhead drip zone covers entire floor)
Wall-top masking for spray methods (tape and paper at ceiling line on wall surface)
Ceiling fixture masking for spray methods (lights, fans, smoke detectors)
Furniture/contents drip covers (in-place — no center-pile, poly draped over)
Opening covers for spray methods (lightweight plastic over doorways/windows)
Dust wipe and vacuum after prep and between coats
Floor vacuum and tool cleaning
Customer walkthrough (occupied homes)

excludes.item: Structural drywall repair (holes, water damage to substrate)

excludes.route_to: Plumber/contractor — moisture SOURCE must be resolved before painting (gate condition)

configuration_dimensions.description: Quality tier controlling coat count, inspection rigor, edge discipline, and interstage sanding. QT2 included as economy refresh tier.
configuration_dimensions.notes: QT2=1 finish coat, relaxed edges, quick inspect, roll-only. QT3=2 coats default, standard edges. QT4=2 coats mandatory, interstage sand, systematic inspect. QT5=2 coats, full interstage, critical raking-light inspect.

configuration_dimensions.description: Primary application technique. Roll is primary for occupied interior ceiling RP. Spray methods available at QT3+.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Roll: QT2-QT5 (most common). spray_backroll: QT3-QT5 (requires full masking). spray: QT4-QT5 (rare in occupied). Spray/backroll coupling constraint enforced.

configuration_dimensions.description: Finish coating sheen level. Flat is default for ceilings. Determines output substrate state.
configuration_dimensions.notes: Flat is standard for residential ceilings. Eggshell for kitchen/bath. Satin/semi-gloss for QT4+ only. Matte excluded (use flat).

configuration_dimensions.description: Universal 3-level condition scale driving prep intensity. Maps from substrate state assessment.
configuration_dimensions.notes: GOOD=SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT (1.0x prep). FAIR=SS_INT_FAILING_PAINT or SS_INT_MOISTURE_DAMAGE (1.3-1.8x prep). POOR=SS_INT_PEELING or SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE (2.0-3.0x prep).

paintable_items.name: Ceiling Field Repaint Surface
paintable_items.counting_rules: Square footage of ceiling surface measured at finished face. Standard room = room width x room length.
paintable_items.notes: Combined prime+finish RP item. _RP suffix avoids collision with existing NC items ITM_CEILING_FIELD_PRIME and ITM_CEILING_FIELD_FINISH (NC specs are phase-split).

paintable_items.name: Wall Edge Cut-In (from ceiling perspective)
paintable_items.counting_rules: Linear footage of ceiling-to-wall junction. Measured at room perimeter.
paintable_items.notes: Reuse existing item from NC ceiling prime. Same physical edge work — freehand cut-in at wall line from ceiling perspective.

variants.notes: Fastest path. Economy refresh on sound ceiling paint. 1 finish coat, no prime. Rental turnover scenario.
BASELINE. Most common residential ceiling repaint. Degloss + 2 finish coats. No prime needed.
Standard repaint on failing/moisture-damaged ceilings. Scrape + feather + spot/full prime + 2 finish coats.
Full remediation. Heavy scrape + full adhesion/stain-block prime + 2 finish coats. Highest prep labor.
Premium refresh. Spray+backroll with interstage sanding. Full masking required.
Premium remediation. Full prep + interstage sand between finish coats.
Maximum effort. Full remediation + critical quality. Near-worst-case labor scenario.

required_paintscope_inputs.description: Total square footage of ceiling surfaces to be repainted
Linear footage of ceiling-to-wall junction for cut-in work and caulk assessment
Full floor area for protection coverage (always full for ceiling work)
Total room count driving per-room fixed tasks (assessment, furniture, fixtures, walkthrough)
Furniture drip protection area in occupied homes (in-place covers)
Condition scale (GOOD/FAIR/POOR) — primary prep intensity driver
Ceiling surface texture (smooth/orange_peel/knockdown/heavy_texture) — drives texture modifier
Ceiling height tier (H1/H2/H3/H4) — drives height modifier. Critical for ceilings — overhead penalty compounds with height.
Interior substrate state (SS_INT_SOUND_PAINT through SS_INT_SMOKE_DAMAGE) — drives primer selection and prep pathway
Pre-1978 home flag — triggers EPA Lead-Safe RRP module
Contamination type (none/mildew/smoke/water_stain/grease) — drives contamination treatment tasks and modifier
Occupancy state (vacant/occupied_crew_handles/occupied_sensitive) — drives furniture protection and customer walkthrough
Lead test result — drives RRP module activation
Ceiling height band for overhead access classification (H1_STANDARD/H2_TALL/H3_HIGH/H4_SCAFFOLD)
Application method selection — drives task activation and protection requirements

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Adhesion Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: Water-based adhesion promoter for previously painted surfaces. Bonds to glossy, chalky, or oil-based existing coatings. Shared with wall RP.

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Stain-Blocking Primer (Shellac)
material_systems_summary.notes: Shellac-based stain blocker (BIN or equivalent). Only product that seals nicotine/smoke. Requires denatured alcohol for tool cleanup.

material_systems_summary.name: Interior Mildew-Resistant Primer
material_systems_summary.notes: Mildew-resistant stain-blocking primer. Applied after biocide treatment and source moisture resolution. Common on bathroom/kitchen ceilings.

material_systems_summary.name: Ceiling Finish — Standard (QT2-QT3)
material_systems_summary.notes: Standard interior ceiling finish. Dead flat sheen. Ceiling-specific formulation with better overhead application properties.

material_systems_summary.name: Ceiling Finish — Premium (QT4)
material_systems_summary.notes: Premium ceiling finish. Higher solids, better hide. Eggshell or satin available for kitchen/bath ceilings.

material_systems_summary.name: Ceiling Finish — Superior (QT5)
material_systems_summary.notes: Superior ceiling finish. Maximum film build, self-leveling. Semi-gloss available for critical spaces.

module_summary.description: Full floor protection (always), furniture drip covers, wall-top masking (spray), ceiling fixture masking (spray), opening covers (spray)
Condition scan, adhesion test, moisture meter, coating ID
Lead test, containment setup, HEPA vacuum, containment removal, waste disposal (conditional: pre-1978)
TSP wash, mildew treatment, scrape, feather, degloss, spackle, sand spackle, caulk perimeter, dust wipe, vacuum dust
Cut-in primer at wall line, roll primer, spray primer, backroll primer, spot prime
Light sand QT4, light sand QT5 (critical), vacuum intercoat dust, inspect between coats, patch defects, spot coat
Cut-in wall R1/R2, roll finish R1/R2, spray finish R1/R2, backroll finish R1/R2, spray finish R2/backroll R2
Remove wall masking, fixture protection, floor teardown, furniture uncover, vacuum floors, clean tools, final inspect (QT2/QT3, QT4, QT5), touchup, customer walkthrough

stacking_partition.prep_pool: condition x contamination x height x texture (max 7.50x)
stacking_partition.never_cross: Prep pool never includes QT. Coating pool never includes condition or contamination. No wall_access modifier for ceilings.
stacking_partition.ceiling_vs_wall_note: No wall_access modifier — overhead access obstruction is irrelevant. Max theoretical stacking lower than wall RP (7.50x vs 9.75x prep, 3.75x vs 4.88x coating).

protection_zones_required.notes: Full-room floor coverage ALWAYS required for ceiling work. Overhead drip zone covers entire floor regardless of application method. No perimeter-only option. Rosin paper on hard floors, plastic on carpet.
Tape and paper applied to wall tops at ceiling line for spray overspray containment. Not needed for roll — ceiling painter cuts into wall freehand.
Stuff and tape ceiling lights, fans, smoke detectors for spray methods. Also recommended for roll at QT4+.
Ceiling-specific: furniture/contents covered IN PLACE with poly sheeting (no center-pile move). Overhead drip protection only. Distinct from wall RP furniture_room (which involves center-pile move).
Lightweight plastic over door and window openings to contain ceiling overspray. Spray methods only.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Ceiling painter establishes wall line via freehand cut-in. No tape/mask on drywall walls per doctrine (cutting from ceiling side). Wall-top masking is for spray overspray, not cut-in accuracy.
If crown molding exists, ceiling line is at crown-to-ceiling junction instead of wall-to-ceiling. Rare in standard residential. Cut-in task applies at whichever junction exists.

valid_input_states.notes: All 5 SS_INT_* states accepted. Each drives distinct prep pathway and primer selection. Ceiling-specific: moisture damage more common (roof leaks, condensation, plumbing above). Smoke damage rises — ceilings accumulate smoke faster than walls.

output_state.notes: All input states normalize to SS_PAINTED_* output after proper prep and coating. Flat is default for ceilings (unlike eggshell for walls).

adjacent_state_protection_rules.notes: Wall-top masking for spray methods only. Roll method: no protection — ceiling painter cuts into wall freehand (same doctrine as wall cutting into ceiling).
If crown exists, tape at crown-to-ceiling junction for spray methods. Roll method: freehand cut-in.

site_condition_rules.notes: Occupied home adds furniture drip covers (in-place) and customer walkthrough. Vacant ceiling RP omits these tasks.
active_moisture is STOP WORK. recently_wet requires extended dry time. Ceiling-specific: roof leaks, condensation, plumbing above.
Contamination type drives TSP wash and biocide treatment activation. Ceiling-specific: kitchen ceilings accumulate grease, bathroom ceilings accumulate mildew.
Per Modifier_Registry. Critical for ceiling work — overhead penalty compounds with height access penalty. H3/H4 require scaffold or baker staging.

cross_spec_coordination.deduplication_note: When ceiling RP and wall RP occur in same room, floor protection is shared (ceiling goes first — full floor already laid). Fixture masking may partially overlap. Assessment can be combined. Estimator should apply cross-spec efficiency factor.
cross_spec_coordination.shared_session_note: Ceiling RP typically scheduled before wall RP in same-room scenarios. Ceiling overspray falls on floor protection (already in place). Wall masking at ceiling line serves dual purpose.

sequencing_notes.production_sequence: Setup (protect) -> Assess (condition) -> RRP (if pre-1978) -> Prep (state-driven) -> Prime (state-driven) -> Interstage (QT4/QT5) -> Finish 1 -> Interstage (QT4/QT5) -> Finish 2 (QT3+) -> Inspect -> Touch-up -> Teardown -> Cleanup -> Customer Walkthrough
sequencing_notes.edge_work: Ceiling-to-wall cut-in is the primary edge work. Freehand cut-in from ceiling side — no tape on drywall walls per doctrine.
sequencing_notes.key_prohibitions: NO spray primer without backroll (adhesion mandatory). NO masking drywall walls at ceiling line (freehand only). NO painting over active moisture. NO latex primer on smoke damage (shellac only). Spot prime ALL spackled/scraped areas regardless of full prime.

relationships.notes: Second interior repaint spec. Combined prime+finish (no separate phases). NC ceiling prime/finish are sibling specs. Adapted from wall RP template with 15-20% overhead penalty and ceiling-specific protection (full floor always, furniture drip covers, no wall access modifier).

sections_used: Shellac stain-blocker mandate for smoke damage
No wall masking for ceiling work
